newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says 1996 German growth could be stronger.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says 1996 German growth could be stronger.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Thursday 1996 German economic growth could be stronger than previous government expectations.
His ministry in April forecast that growth for the full year would be 0.75 percent.
"An increasing number of economic indicators speak for a continuation of the economic revival," Rexrodt said.

Gross domestic product rose 1.2 percent in the second quarter of 1996 from the year-earlier period, erasing the declines of the previous quarter. Growth in the first half was 0.7 percent from a year earlier.
The rebound was due to core growth as well as seasonal recovery from the unusually severe winter, Rexrodt said.
Low interest rates, moderate wage agreements, stable prices and a retreat in the mark's overvaluation all contributed to a recovery of business confidence.

Incoming orders expanded, boosting industrial production and capacity utilisation. Construction demand remained weak, but the economy is back on course for growth in the medium term, Rexrodt said. Labour market conditions remained unsatisfactory, and no near-term relief was visible, he said.
"More effort at flexibility and an accelerated economic development are indispensable fro an improvement in the labour market," he said.
The services sector continued its expansion, which had been uninterrupted by the weak phase in the broader economy.
